messages:
sam: After running the macOS Homebrew installer on WSL2 (weird combo, I know), my shell init got written into both ~/.bashrc and ~/.profile. Now when I run `redwoodctl localserve` the CLI gets stuck in an auth retry loop. It prints `auth: retrying` repeatedly and nothing completes. Anyone familiar?

maria: Oof. Can you paste the exact appended blocks from both files? Duplicate init is a common root cause.

sam: Heres what was appended to both: 
```
# redwoodctl init
source ~/.redwood/profile
export REDWOOD_PROFILE=default
```
And running `ps aux | grep auth-agent` shows two auth-agent processes. `redwoodctl auth status` says `auth: pending`.

jonathan: That explains it. Two agents racing for the same device/socket can cause the device busy error and retries. What do the localserve logs show?

sam: Logs show: 
```
[2025-11-02T08:14:12Z] auth-agent starting
[2025-11-02T08:14:12Z] opening token device /run/user/1000/redwood.token
[2025-11-02T08:14:14Z] auth: retrying (err: device busy)
[2025-11-02T08:14:16Z] auth: retrying (err: device busy)
```

ali: Workaround: remove one of the duplicated blocks (I removed from ~/.profile) and restart the shell. Alternatively add an idempotency guard: 
```sh
if [ -z "$REDWOOD_INIT_DONE" ]; then
  export REDWOOD_INIT_DONE=1
  source ~/.redwood/profile
fi
```

maria: Better: create a marker `~/.redwood/initialized` at postinstall and have the init logic check for it before appending/sourcing. Also the installer should prefer the interactive login rc: on bash -> ~/.bashrc, on zsh -> ~/.zshrc, etc.

jonathan: I'll add a migration command `redwoodctl diagnose-init` that detects multiple redwood blocks, prints friendly remediation steps, and optionally fixes them when run with `--apply`. Diagnostic output example: 
```
Detected redwoodctl init in: ~/.bashrc, ~/.profile
Recommended: keep ~/.bashrc entry, remove from ~/.profile
Run: redwoodctl diagnose-init --apply to auto-remove duplicates
```

sam: Removing the duplicate block fixed my issue. Sharing steps I used in case support needs them: 
1) `grep -n "redwoodctl init" ~/.bashrc ~/.profile`
2) edit the file that you want to remove the block from (I removed from ~/.profile)
3) `pkill -f auth-agent` then re-run `redwoodctl login`

maria: Filed DX-4897 and linked your repro, thanks @sam. We'll patch the installer to be idempotent and add the diagnostic tool. Also adding an integration test that simulates multiple rc sources on WSL.

ali: Temporary UX patch: if installer detects WSL, append only to the more commonly sourced rc (bashrc for bash) and print a notice: "WSL detected: we added shell init to ~/.bashrc. If you see duplicate entries in other files run `redwoodctl diagnose-init`."

sam: Thanks all, saved me a lot of time. Posting this here because I searched and didn't find an existing thread with the same combo.

devex-bot: Ticket DX-4897 created: "installer: make shell-init idempotent; add diagnose-init; update WSL messaging." Assigned to @maria and @jonathan.
